scenes.text: You reach a hill, and suddenly every pedal stroke feels heavy. Your legs strain, but the bike barely seems to move.
In a lower gear, one full turn of the pedals moves the bike a shorter distance. That means less force at the pedals.
You'll need more pedal turns to climb the same hill. You're trading speed for an effort you can sustain, so keep a comfortable rhythm.
Before the hill begins, shift into a lower gear while pedaling lightly. Ease the pressure as you make the shift.
